texts: My grandmother fasted so strictly for the temple festival that she fell ill, then feasted the next day, and the old grinder stood idle while she recovered, and she finally said, neither too much nor too little.
temple, grindstone, balance
At the temple too much zeal is as bad as none; the grindstone grinds fine only at a measured pace.

Write a doha about the devotee at the temple who fasts too hard and feasts too much, and the grindstone that works nicely only at a steady measured turn, teaching that the middle way in all things is best.
doha w a temple and a grindstone - not too much not too little, even in devotion
The cloth sheet too tightly drawn will tear, too loosely drawn will slip; hold it in the middle and rest.
doha w a cloth sheet - pull it too tight it rips, too loose it falls, find the middle
cloth sheet, middle path
Write a doha about a cloth sheet that tears if stretched too tight and slips off if held too loosely, teaching that in all matters of life the wise find the middle path and avoid excess either way.
My mother-in-law keeps the bedsheet pulled so tight on the mattress that it rips every month, while my sister lets hers hang off the bed, and my aunt says there is a right amount in everything.
Write a Kabir-style doha saying that too much talking is bad and too much silence is also bad, too much of anything is harmful, and the wise person knows how much is enough in each thing.

My uncle talks nonstop at every family gathering until people leave, and his wife, who is the opposite, says nothing for days, and my grandmother says both are wrong and the right amount is in between.
doha on not talking too much and not being too quiet either, balance
neither too much nor little
Too much speech wearies the world, too much silence starves it; the wise know the measure.
doha about eating just enough, i overeat then starve myself on diets
eat in measure
Too full is a sickness and too empty is a sickness; seat thyself in the middle of the measure.
After years of crash diets followed by binges, my dietitian advised me to simply eat what I need at regular times, and I realise now that I was swinging between two extremes.
Please write a doha that advises eating neither too little nor too much, for the glutton and the faster alike suffer, and the one who eats in measure keeps both body and mind healthy.

The cloud poured on our village for three weeks until the fields were flooded, then not a drop for months, and the grain merchant checking his scales said that too much and too little are equally ruinous.
doha w a cloud and scales - too much rain floods, too little dries, nature needs balance

I'd love a doha about the cloud that rains too heavily one season and not at all in another, and the scales that must balance exactly, teaching that excess in either direction brings ruin and the middle way is wisest.
cloud, scales, balance
Too much the cloud pours and the fields drown; too little, they parch; the scales of the wise rest evenly.
My son studies sixteen hours a day before exams and then does nothing for a week afterwards, and I told him that steady and moderate effort throughout is wiser than extremes.
Neither the storm nor the stillness serves; walk the middle road, O child, and reach the end.
doha on avoiding extremes in work and rest
avoid extremes
Write a doha for people who go to extremes, working like mad and then collapsing, saying that the wise follow a measured pace in all they do and keep their strength for the whole journey.
The old boatman never rowed too hard or too lazily, just at a steady pace, and he reached the far side each day with strength to spare, while the young men who sprinted tired halfway.
Too hard the oar and the boat tires, too soft and it drifts; the wise boatman rows in measure.
doha w a boat - row too hard u get tired, too slow u drift, steady wins
Write a doha about the boat that is rowed too fast and tires its crew, or too slowly and drifts from its course, teaching that moderation in effort is the secret of reaching the destination.
boat, steady pace
Sow the seed in measure and let the lute be plucked in measure; too much of either spoils the song.
My teacher said that a farmer who sows too many seeds in one patch gets nothing, and a musician who plucks his one-string lute too long goes sour, and moderation is the secret of both.
doha w a seed and a one-string lute - too much of either is a waste, keep it moderate

Give me a doha about the farmer who sows seed in measure and the musician who plays his one-string lute in measure, teaching that even good things in excess spoil, and that restraint is the heart of every art.
seed, lute, restraint
The elephant that eats too much seed grows heavy and slow; the one that eats in measure walks tall and far.
doha w a seed and an elephant - eating too many seeds makes the elephant sick, moderation is key

Write a doha about an elephant that eats too much seed and falls ill, while the one that eats in measure lives long and strong, teaching that restraint in appetite is the foundation of health and strength.
The mahout told us the elephant fell sick because it ate sacks of seed in a single day, and since then he feeds it a fixed small portion, and it has been strong for years.
elephant, seed, measure
traveller, palace, enough
The traveller who stops at every palace never arrives, and the one who never rests falls; wisdom is in measure.
doha w a traveller and a palace - dont rush thru the trip, dont stay forever at the palace, find the middle

Write a doha about a traveller who neither lingers too long at the palace nor hurries past without rest, teaching that moderation in travel and in life is wisest, avoiding both indulgence and exhaustion.
On my trip I stayed too long at a fancy palace hotel and then rushed through the rest of the route, and I came home exhausted and broke, and my father said I should have found the middle.
My brother started going to the gym six hours a day and ended up with a broken body, a skeleton of his former strength, and the trainer told him that moderation builds more than extremes.
The skeleton of the over-strained shows what excess costs; the wise take each task in measure.
doha w a skeleton - overdoing it will leave u a skeleton, restraint is smarter

A doha, please, about the man who starves himself in excess of devotion until he is no more than a skeleton, teaching that extremes of any kind ruin the body and mind, and that the wise keep to the middle.
skeleton, overdoing

At the lotus pond the dew was heavy all night and then the heat scorched the next day, and the lotus drooped from both, and the gardener told us a flower likes a little of everything and not too much.
Write a doha about the lotus that suffers if it gets too much dew or too little, teaching that in every aspect of life the right amount is the key and that excess in any direction brings loss.
Too much dew drowns the lotus, too little dries it; let the moderate hour bring the bloom.
doha w dew and a lotus - too much dew too little dew, lotus needs just right
dew, lotus, just enough

Please write a doha about the foolishness of spending too much, saving too little, or the reverse, teaching that in the handling of money and everything else the middle way avoids both waste and miserliness.
The spendthrift and the miser are brothers in folly; the wise man keeps his hand open only as wide as need.
My cousin spends his whole salary the day it arrives and then borrows, while my uncle never spends a rupee on himself even when ill, and my mother says both are wrong and the answer is in between.
spend in measure
doha on spending wisely, not too stingy not too wasteful
doha w a cremation ground - too much grief also isnt good, mourn in measure

Write a doha about mourning at the cremation ground, teaching that grief in excess harms the living as much as no grief at all, and that the wise mourn in measure and then return to life with a steady heart.
cremation ground, mourn in measure
After my brother's cremation I could neither eat nor cry nor speak for weeks, until my aunt gently said that sorrow too has a right measure and that I must also live.
At the cremation ground the wise weep, but only as much as the day demands, and then they turn to life again.
My friend sleeps ten hours on weekends and four on weekdays, and he is always irritable and tired, and his grandfather says that a fixed moderate sleep every night is the best medicine.
sleep in measure
Need a doha about sleep taken in the right measure, for too much sleep dulls the mind and too little frays it, teaching that the wise keep a steady rhythm of rest and work and avoid excess in either.
doha on a balanced sleep schedule and not extremes
Too much sleep dulls the wit, too little sharpens only the temper; the wise take rest in measure.
The stone too heavy sinks the cage, too light it flies away; let the weight be measured in all things.
doha w a stone and a cage - too heavy a stone breaks the cage, too light does nothing, balance
Write a doha about a stone placed on a cage which breaks it if it is too heavy and does nothing if too light, teaching that in all matters of strictness and discipline, moderation is the right way.
stone, cage, right weight
My father put a stone on the cage to hold its latch, but it was so heavy the cage bent, and a lighter one did nothing, so he found the one that fit, which is true of all rules.
crossroads, chakor, balance
doha w a crossroads and a chakor - dont go too far one way, find the middle path at the crossroads
At the crossroads of two life choices I kept swinging between total sacrifice and total indulgence like a chakor bird confused, until my guru said the middle path is the real path.
Write a doha about a traveller who stands at a crossroads with a chakor bird flying overhead and chooses the middle path between two extremes, teaching that moderation avoids the ruin of both sides.
At the crossroads the chakor flies the middle sky; neither the heights nor the depths, but the measured way.
My grandmother taught me that a seed needs a little water, not too much and not too little, and said the same is true of love and discipline with children.
Write a doha about the gardener who gives a seed the right amount of water and warmth, no more and no less, teaching that moderation in care and discipline is the way to growth.
doha w a seed - too much water drowns, too little dries, the right amount is key
Too much water drowns the seed, too little leaves it dry; the loving hand gives in measure.
seed, just enough
grindstone, measured grain
Feed the grindstone too much and it jams, too little and it idles; the wise grinder feeds in measure.
My grandmother always said to put just a handful at a time on the grindstone, since too much clogs it and too little wastes the effort, and she applied the same rule to her cooking and her words.
Write a doha about the grindstone that jams when overloaded and idles when underfed, teaching that in work and in life one should neither take on too much nor too little, but keep to the middle way.
doha w a grindstone - too much grain jams it, too little wastes it, moderation
The loom too tightly strung will snap; too loose, it weaves nothing; the weaver tunes it in measure.
loom, right tension
My uncle the weaver says that if the loom is strung too tight the fibres snap and if too loose the weave is useless, and he applies the same lesson to how he lives his whole life.

Please give me a couplet about the weaver whose loom must be strung neither too tight nor too loose to weave nicely, teaching that the middle way, avoiding strictness and laxity, is the way to a balanced life.
doha w a weaver's loom - not too tight not too loose, just right, like life
Pray at the mosque in measure, neither too much nor too little; the wise keep a steady devotion without excess.
Write a doha about the devotee at the mosque who prays so long that he neglects his family and others who never pray at all, teaching that moderation in devotion is the path of the wise.
doha w a mosque - dont overdo the rituals or ignore them, find a balance
mosque, balanced devotion
My neighbour spends every waking hour in the mosque and has neglected his children, while his brother never goes at all, and the elders told them that devotion, like everything, is best in measure.
My mother cooked bitter gourd for us once a week, never daily and never never, because she said that medicine in excess is poison and in lack is neglect.
The bitter gourd is medicine in measure and poison in excess; so is every virtue overdone.
doha w bitter gourd - healthy in small amount, bad in excess, same as everything

Write a doha about the bitter gourd, which heals when taken in moderation but harms when taken in excess, teaching that even good things must be used in measure, for excess turns medicine into poison.
bitter gourd, right dose
doha w a pearl - dont chase too many pearls or ignore them, enough is enough
The diver who takes too many pearls drowns; the one who takes but a few returns to the shore.
pearl, take enough

My uncle was a pearl trader who once packed a thousand pearls in a single load and lost them all in a flood, while his moderate brother with a hundred got home safe, and the lesson stayed with the family.

I'd love a doha about the pearl diver who grows greedy and takes too many pearls in a single dive and is lost, while another who takes only what he needs returns safely, teaching moderation in desire.
musk deer, priest, restraint
The musk deer runs too far for the scent within; the priest prays too long for the god within; the wise do both in measure.

My uncle, a priest, used to wander all over the wilderness like a musk deer in search of enlightenment and ruined his health, until his own teacher said that seeking too hard is as bad as not seeking at all.
doha w a musk deer and a priest - dont over search or over pray, find the balance
Write a doha about the musk deer that wears itself out searching too far and the priest who wears himself out praying too long, both showing that moderation in seeking brings more than excess.
The stone on the cremation ground warns us: too much grief breaks the heart, too little leaves it stone; walk the middle road.

Write a doha about a stone at the cremation ground that teaches mourners that neither too much grief nor too little is right, and that the wise follow a middle path of measured feeling and calm remembrance.
At my mother's cremation I felt like a stone, feeling nothing, and later I broke down for days, and the elder told me that there is a measure in grief, and neither extreme is the path.
doha w a stone and a cremation ground - dont break down completely or go stone cold, find the balance in grief
stone, cremation ground, balance
enough is enough
doha on knowing when to stop, i always overdo things
The wise man knows where to put the full stop; the fool pours on till the vessel spills.

Give me a doha for the person who always overdoes everything, whether work, play, gifts or advice, teaching that the wise know when enough is enough and stop at the right measure, sparing both themselves and others.
My aunt always serves her guests until they cannot eat, then wonders why they dread her invitations, and my mother says that a good host knows the right measure, which is a little less than too much.

Write a doha about the washerman who rubs the garment too hard and tears it, or too lightly and leaves it dirty, and the bee that takes just enough honey from each flower, teaching the way of the wise.
The washerman at our ghat never beats the clothes too hard or too gently, and a bee hovered about him as if admiring his measure, and my grandmother said that is how to do every job.
The washerman scrubs in measure and the bee takes in measure; so the world is kept in balance.
washerman, bee, moderation
doha w a washerman and a bee - both take the right amount, no more, no less
Too fierce a heat reduces all to ash and too little cooks nothing; the net is cast in measure, and the catch is just.
Write a doha about the heat that reduces everything to ash when too fierce and cooks nothing when too weak, and the net that must be cast in measure, teaching that moderation keeps life in balance.
My uncle turned the stove up so high that the food turned to ash, then too low so it stayed raw, while his net hung forgotten, and his wife said cooking, like life, needs a measured heat.
doha w ash and a net - too much heat gives ash, cast the net in measure too
ash, net, measure

A doha, please, about the thief who steals a little at first and then too much and ends up caught, teaching that restraint in desire saves a man from ruin, and even a rogue would do wisely to learn it.
The thief who takes a little goes free; the greedy thief takes all and is taken.
doha w a thief - he got caught cuz he took too much, if he'd been moderate he'd have been fine, lol
thief, took too much
A pickpocket in our town would take just a little from many people and was never caught for years, until he grew greedy and took a whole purse, and the police arrested him within the week.
Between the too much and the too little lies the road of the wise; walk it, and be at peace.
the middle way
doha about the middle path in life, extremes are exhausting
After years of swinging between workaholism and burnout, I started working steady hours and resting steadily, and my life has finally become calm in a way that I did not think possible.

Please write a doha that praises the middle way in life, the path between indulgence and austerity, between haste and sloth, where the wise walk with calm and steady strides and never exhaust themselves.

Write a doha about the tree that grows strong when it gets just enough water and sunlight and withers when it gets too much or too little, teaching that moderation in all nourishment is the secret of health.
doha w a tree - too much water too little water, the tree wants just enough, same for us
The tree thrives on measure; too much drowns its roots, too little dries its leaves, and the middle feeds it.
My father pruned our tree exactly twice a year, never more, never less, and it gave fruit every season, while the neighbour's tree, cut daily, died, and he said the wise know where to stop.
tree, just enough
My nutritionist friend says that exercise, coffee, sleep and even good things like fruit are best in moderate amounts, and that the human body is built to love balance.
Need a doha for people who overdo even healthy things like exercise or fasting or study, saying that anything taken to excess becomes harmful, and that the best health is in moderation in all things.
even good things, in measure
Even nectar becomes poison in excess; take of every good thing only as much as is needed.
doha: too much of a good thing is bad, restraint in all things
Write a doha about the moth that goes too close to the light and is destroyed, but if it kept a measured distance it would live, teaching that excess in desire and attachment leads to ruin.
doha w a moth - it goes too close to the light and dies, should have kept a distance
moth, too close

My little cousin kept going nearer the bulb to read until her hair singed, and a moth beating against the glass next to her made my aunt say that those who go too close get hurt, and moderation is wisdom.
The moth that circles the light at a measured distance lives; the one that wants all of it dies.
doha on not getting too attached or too cold in relationships, find the balance
love in measure
Love that clings suffocates, love that cools starves; the wise love with an open hand.
Write a doha about love between people which should be neither suffocating nor cold, teaching that in all relationships the middle way of warm but unclinging affection is the path of the wise.
My ex was so clingy he called me thirty times a day, and then I dated a man so distant he forgot my birthday, and I realised that what I want is something in the middle.
The skeleton of the miser and the skeleton of the glutton are equal; the wise man's body is kept sound by measure.
doha w a skeleton - starving or stuffing myself both end up the same, bad
skeleton, avoid extremes

My two uncles lived at extremes, one starving himself for religion and the other feasting without limit, and both ended up skeletal in different ways, while my father who ate and fasted moderately lived to ninety.

Could you do a doha about the skeleton that reminds us that the miser who starves himself and the glutton who destroys himself end in the same place, and that the wise keep their appetites in measure and live long.

Write a doha for a person who gets very excited by things and gives them everything at first, then loses interest and drops them, teaching that steady and measured enthusiasm lasts longer than a blazing start.
steady enthusiasm
doha on not burning out, i start strong and quit all the time
The fervour that leaps at the start is gone by evening; the steady habit endures the whole year.
I start every hobby with great fervour and buy everything for it, then quit within a month, and my wife says that a gentle start with a steady pace would have taken me much further.
A priest in our village fasted three days a week and then overate on the others, and his health suffered, until an old woman at the village square told him that even devotion has to be measured.
priest, balanced devotion
doha w a priest - dont overdo fasting or overeat after, moderation in religion too
Write a doha about a priest who swings between extremes of fasting and feasting and is made ill by both, teaching that restraint and measure in even religious practice is the way to health and peace.
The priest who fasts too hard feasts too long; the wise priest eats in measure and prays in measure.

Please give me a couplet about the paras of the alchemist, which turns metal to treasure only when used in measure, and the dew that nourishes the plant only when light, teaching that measure is the key to every blessing.
After a heavy dew the paras-like glow of the garden vanished by noon, and my gardener said everything extreme passes quickly and only the measured keeps, and that is how he plans his work.
doha w the paras and dew - too much and it ruins, the right measure brings the blessing
The dew in measure feeds the plant, the paras in measure feeds the man; but excess is the ruin of both.
paras, dew, in measure
Neither the feast nor the fast, neither the shout nor the hush; between them runs the road of peace.
My grandfather, who lived to a hundred, said his secret was never doing anything too much, no excess of food, work, sleep, anger or even joy, and he never regretted it.

Please write a doha about a long and healthy life that comes to those who practise restraint in all things, avoiding excess in eating, working, sleeping, speaking and feeling, and walking always in the middle.
live in moderation
doha about living moderately for a long and peaceful life
arrow, measured aim
The arrow drawn too far snaps the bow, drawn too little falls short; the archer draws in measure.
My archery coach taught us never to pull the arrow back too far or too little, and to use the right strength at every shot, and he said that this rule applies to everything.
doha w an arrow - pull the bow too far it breaks, too little it falls short, balance
Write a doha about the archer who draws his bow neither too far nor too little, sending the arrow in measure to the mark, teaching that moderation in effort is the secret of hitting any target.
The village well gave sweet water when drawn moderately, but when everyone drew from it day and night it went dry, and the elders called a meeting on sharing it fairly and using it in measure.
well, draw in measure

Write a doha about the well that gives water as long as it is drawn from in measure and goes dry when overdrawn, teaching that restraint in taking from nature and from others preserves the source for all.
doha w a well - dont overuse it or it dries up, use only what u need
The well gives to the moderate and fails the greedy; draw only what thy need requires.
Zeal in measure is wisdom but zeal poured out all at once is ruin; measure thy fervour as the cook measures his hand.
doha on not going overboard with enthusiasm, i always burn out
measured zeal

When my sister got engaged she planned a week of ceremonies and spent three years of savings, and the couple were exhausted and in debt by the end, and the elders said that joy too is best in measure.

I'd love a doha for people who throw all their energy and resources into a single celebration or effort and are left exhausted, teaching that restraint in enthusiasm leaves strength for the long road ahead.

Write a doha about a bridge that holds firm when its load is moderate and collapses when overloaded, teaching that even the strongest things must be used in measure and that moderation protects all that we build.
bridge, load in measure
doha w a bridge - overloaded and it collapses, only so much weight it can take
The old bridge near our village could carry a cart or two, but when everyone crowded onto it for the festival it creaked and nearly gave way, and the engineer said everything has a safe measure.
The bridge bears a measured load; heaped too high it falls, and the crossers fall with it.
Write a doha about the lock on a treasure that must be neither too loose nor too tight, and a man who guards his wealth with measured care, teaching that this avoids both neglect and obsession.
The lock too loose invites the intruder, the lock too tight chokes the hand; the wise keep their treasure with measured care.
lock, measured care
doha w a lock - dont be paranoid or careless about ur stuff, moderate security
My neighbour never locks his place and was robbed twice, while another locks his seven times and cannot find the key in the morning, and my father says safety, like everything, wants moderation.

The musk deer that runs about the wild searching for its own scent wears itself out, and my meditation teacher says that seeking too hard is as exhausting as never seeking, and the answer is steady practice.
Write a doha about the musk deer that wears itself out running everywhere in search of a scent that lies within, teaching that moderation even in seeking brings more peace than a restless chase.
musk deer, seek in measure
The musk deer races through the wild and tires; a measured step would have found the scent within.
doha w a musk deer - dont chase so hard, a steady pace finds it
Neither too tight a hold nor too loose a drift; the wise heart carries its cares in the middle.
My father worked eighteen hours a day for twenty years and then retired and slept for six months, and he says he regrets both extremes and wishes he had lived steadily.
doha on living a balanced life instead of working like crazy and then crashing
Write a doha for a person who goes between overwork and total collapse in life, teaching that the wise live a steady, balanced life with regular rest and regular work, avoiding the ruin of extremes.
steady life
Neither the heat of passion nor the cold of denial; the wise soul keeps a gentle temperate heart.
My parents were extremely strict with me and I rebelled wildly, so when I became a parent I tried to be neither strict nor lax, but kind and firm, and my daughter has turned out fine.
doha on parenting in the middle, not too strict not too loose

A doha, please, for parents on raising children, saying that too much strictness breeds rebellion and too much indulgence breeds ruin, and that the wise parent walks the middle path of love combined with firmness.
parenting in measure
mosque, tongue, restraint
The man who talks loudly at the mosque disturbs everyone, and his brother who never speaks at all troubles his family, and the imam's advice to both is to use the tongue in moderation.
The tongue that prays too loud at the mosque disturbs the quiet, the tongue that is always silent shames the heart; the wise speak in measure.
doha w a mosque and a tongue - dont talk too much, dont stay too silent, balance
Write a doha about the tongue that should neither talk too much in the mosque nor stay silent when words are needed, teaching that restraint and restraint in speech are the mark of a wise devotee.

The tailor's needle must be neither too sharp nor too blunt, and the merchant's scales neither too heavy nor too light, my grandfather said, and so also a man's judgement, which must be balanced in every case.

Write a doha about a needle that must be neither too fine nor too coarse and the scales that must balance exactly, teaching that in all craft and judgement the middle way avoids excess and brings fair results.
doha w a needle and scales - needle not too thick not too thin, scales balanced, life needs moderation
needle, scales, balance
The needle too coarse tears and too fine breaks; the scales weigh true only when balanced.
furnace, tree, balanced heat
doha w a furnace and a tree - too hot burns the tree, too cold it wont grow, moderate heat
Too near the furnace the tree is scorched, too far it freezes; the wise plant at a measured distance.
Need a doha about the tree placed near a furnace which dies if too near and withers if too far, teaching that moderation in closeness to heat and passion preserves life and growth for all.
My grandmother planted her mango tree at a fair distance from the brick furnace, neither too close nor too far, and she said even a tree knows that excess heat kills and too little leaves it weak.
